mappedContracts.statement: Create a canonical machine-readable implementation contract derived from this prompt and make it the binding source of truth for all subsequent work.
acceptanceCriteria: The contract records this prompt's SHA-256, every contract ID, phase, track, task, dependency decision, acceptance criterion, GitHub issue reference, Conductor path, status, evidence, and exception.
A deterministic validator fails on missing mappings, duplicate IDs, invalid states, orphaned tasks, unapproved scope changes, or completion without evidence.
Every implementation PR runs the contract validator as a required check.

mappedContracts.statement: Use one declarative command/capability registry to generate CLI, MCP, schemas, completions, documentation, safety classifications, and coverage metadata.
acceptanceCriteria: Each capability records ID, input/output schemas, transport, stability, evidence, read/write class, destructive/idempotent hints, approval requirement, and fallback.
Generated artefacts are drift-checked in CI.
No manual duplicate command catalogue remains.

mappedContracts.statement: Every MCP tool has accurate readOnly, destructive, idempotent, and open-world annotations, strong descriptions, bounded schemas, and safe structured errors.
acceptanceCriteria: Annotation drift is generated from the capability registry and checked.
No write tool is exposed without the common mutation contract.

mappedContracts.statement: Generate README feature tables, command documentation, MCP catalogues, schemas, safety classifications, support matrix, and roadmap status from executable sources of truth.
acceptanceCriteria: No stale version, capability, quality, or completion claim remains.
Lifecycle labels distinguish planned, implemented, contract-verified, simulator-verified, canary-verified, production-observed, and deprecated.
